name: Mumbai Street Perception: Four Qualities from 1 to 5
description:
Method replication: participants rate 20 Mumbai street scenes, each shown as six views around one spot, on how beautiful, boring, lively and safe the place looks, from 1 to 5; the images are not the paper's stimuli (69 newly fetched Google Street View spots across Mumbai City and the suburbs, six views at 60° steps, 60° field of view, 15° upward pitch as in the paper).

Original study: Chauhan, Baswal & Kumar (2025), International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation 144, 104932. Points every 100 m on about 6,751 km of roads in Mumbai City, Mumbai Suburban and part of Thane gave 120,287 locations, each captured as six Google Street View images. In a voluntary survey (participants aged 20–65, 60% men), 280 images were each rated by five people on beauty, boredom, liveliness and safety on a 1–5 scale (1,000 responses). Models trained on Place Pulse 2.0 and the Mumbai ratings fed perception scores into pedestrian route planning.

Differences from the original study: (1) the paper's question wording is shown only in its Figure 6, so the item labels and end labels ("1 = not at all", "5 = very") are written for this template; (2) 20 scenes per participant at random, as the paper does not say how many each person rated; (3) the six views are arranged in a 3 × 2 grid.
author: Chauhan, Baswal & Kumar
